Hi Ana — thanks for flagging this. Short answer: trial credits are applied at invoicing time, but there are a few edge cases that can cause a charge to appear.

Quick checklist I ran through:
- Trial credits are tied to the account ID; if you created multiple projects or API keys under a different email they may not have been covered.
- Credits are used until they are exhausted; if you hit a large burst (e.g., load testing) they can deplete mid-cycle.
- VAT lines can appear separately from credits — credits reduce the taxable base, but VAT calculation still runs depending on whether we have a valid EU VAT ID on file.

I pulled invoice #4532 and attached our trial policy summary (trial-policy.pdf). Can you confirm: which account/email the team used for API calls (any non-@deltaworks sub-accounts?), and whether you have already submitted your VAT ID to our billing portal? If you can reply with the VAT number and the account/project id I will escalate immediately.

In the meantime I’ve looped in Laura from billing who can provide a breakdown and, if we determine an error, issue a promotional credit or refund while we investigate.

Apologies for the hassle — we’ll sort this out.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Ana — thanks, and sorry for the confusion. I pulled invoice #4532 (link: https://app.redwood.ai/billing/invoices/4532) and included a line-by-line export below.

Summary:
- Invoice subtotal (token usage): €180.00
- Trial credits applied: -€150.00
- Taxable amount: €30.00
- VAT (21% NL): €6.30
- Total due: €36.30 (rounded on invoice display)

Two notes on why you still see a charge:
1) The trial credits covered most usage but not the entire subtotal — there was a residual taxable amount of €30 after credits.
2) VAT is calculated on the residual amount after credits. If you are a B2B company with a valid EU VAT ID and you provided it at signup or uploaded it to the billing portal, we should not charge VAT (reverse charge applies). I don’t see a VAT ID on file for the account email you provided, which is why VAT appears here.

Next steps I can take for you (pick one):
- If you provide your EU VAT number now, we can reissue the invoice without VAT and apply a one-time credit for the VAT portion (€6.30).
- If the residual usage (€36.30) should also be covered by a promotional extension, we can apply a one-off promotional credit equal to the full amount while we investigate the underlying API key mapping.

I’ve temporarily placed a billing hold on the invoice so finance won’t auto-charge until this is resolved. Please reply with the VAT number (format NL########B##) and let us know if you want the full promotional credit and a 30-day trial extension.

Thanks — looping in Neha from finance operations in case we need to process the credit manually.

Regards,
